title: Elements of Sampling Survey
text: Welcome to the course materials for STAT 348: Sampling Survey. Each chapter below opens its slides in a new window.

title: Elements of Sampling Survey
text:
Chapters

Introduction to Sampling Surveys — overview of survey sampling, target populations vs. sampled populations, sampling frames, and sources of error
General Sampling Concepts — probability sampling designs, inclusion probabilities, sampling weights, and the Horvitz-Thompson estimator
Simple Random Sampling (SRS) — SRS with and without replacement, estimation of population means, totals, and proportions, finite population corrections, and variance estimation
Stratified Sampling — principles of stratification, estimation across strata, proportional allocation, Neyman/optimal allocation, and variance reduction
Ratio and Regression Estimation — utilizing auxiliary information, ratio estimators, linear regression estimators, and relative efficiency
Cluster Sampling — single-stage and two-stage cluster designs, intra-cluster correlation, design effects, and cost-variance optimization
Unequal Probability Sampling — sampling with probability proportional to size (PPS), the Hansen-Hurwitz estimator, and applications in complex survey designs

title: Elements of Sampling Survey
text:
About the slides
The slides are written in Quarto and rendered with reveal.js. Every figure is drawn in R at render time, and the R code that produces a result is shown on the slide when the computation itself is the point; for illustrative figures the code is hidden but available in the source. Each example is self-contained: a data set is simulated or sampled with a fixed seed, so all numbers reported on the slides can be reproduced exactly by re-rendering. Where a method has a known failure mode (such as bias in ratio estimators for small samples), the slides show it rather than describe it, with a working example and a diagnostic. Derivations are kept on the slides in full, split across slides where they are long, and every lecture ends with a summary that connects the sampling design to the ones before and after it.
